judge.vsCurrent: No. At play size (the 64 px sprite and the s4 sheet) the arch is a muddy brown post-and-lintel with salt-and-pepper specks: no readable blocks, no lit top band, no coherent seams, stalactites invisible, whereas the code-built cave in kit-cave-tiers-viewports.jpg / hd2d-desktop-trainer.jpg shows chunky individually readable courses with lit tops, crisp dark seams and one consistent texel size. The only things the kit genuinely cannot make here (a continuous rounded opening rim, fused stalactites) are exactly the things that do not survive 64 px, so the piece gives up the kit's strengths without buying anything visible.
strengths: The pipeline itself is solid and honest: deterministic 11 s run, every gate scripted (5000 tris, 101.9 KB packed, 7 on-ramp colours, density 15.69-16.0, 1 mesh/1 material/1 draw call, doubleSided false, NEAREST sampler, EXT_meshopt only), manifest with hashes, and a self-report that correctly flags the camouflage problem instead of self-attesting.

One watertight SDF skin: no balloon-animal seams where the lintel meets the pillars or where the stalactites root into the span; the opening rim is rounded continuously, which stacked boxes cannot do.
Palette discipline is right: the atlas is strictly the caveStone ramp, mips are mode-halved so no off-palette colours leak, and the GLB round-trips in three r180 with 0 console errors.
At beauty-render scale the r1 (rounded plates) and r3b (chisel facets) variants do show some chunky plate structure; the ingredients for a good read exist in the high poly and in the form/AO masks.
The brief, budgets and refusal list were followed; the piece sits on y=0 at the specified 3.0 x 1.0 x 2.4 slot with bbox deviation 1.2 %.
weaknesses: Atlas reads as camouflage noise: 1,601 UV islands at 47 % fill means ~19 texels per island, smaller than a single rock feature, so no shade feature can span an island and the per-texel percentile rules scatter lone dark/light texels; at 64 px this is salt-and-pepper over flat brown.

No directional lighting is baked: the value term is 0.65*normal.z + 0.35*(1-AO), so every vertical face lands in the same mid shade regardless of whether it faces the key light; shade histogram is 70 % in ramp[3..4] with 0.7 % in the lit shade; the sprite is darker and flatter than any kit wall next to it.

Displacement detail is sub-texel (plate 0.03 units = 0.5 texel, crack 0.05 = 0.8 texel) and then erased by --low-voxel 0.1 + decimate; the low is a pillowy blob (fillet 4) and its facets are what fragment the UVs.

Silhouette: boxy pillars + flat lintel + a vertical-ellipse cut reads as a squarish keyhole doorway; stalactites are 0.18-0.23-radius cones that come out as 2-3 px nubs at 64 px and merge into a dark smear.

Self-assessment measures the wrong things: all automated gates passed while the visual target failed; no island-count, blob-size, lit-top-share or silhouette gate; the 64 px sprite shot underestimates the game's on-screen size (~60-65 px per unit on desktop).
AO distance 0.7 with the floor present smears cavity into broad dark feet rather than crisp seams.
skillFixes: compose.py + bake_masks.py: stop composing per texel; bake a world-position pass and a key-light term; paint world-space cells of 3-5 texels (one flat tone per cell from form + key, a 1-texel lit top edge, a 1-texel dark lower edge), apply cavity/lip per cell, keep the orphan clean-up; add blob/orphan statistics to --check.
uv_blocks.py / uv_check.py / SKILL.md S4: an island gate or a reachable way to larger islands; document that island count, not density, killed the read.

piece_template.py + gn.py + modelling.md: express displacement in texels and keep it in the low (plate >= 0.125, crack >= 0.1, plates 6-10 texels, fillet 2, chisel default); add a kit.courses() blockout helper so arena pieces start as stacked blocks.

shoot.mjs + viewer.html: judge at the game's pixel scale (--ppu 64 desktop, 36 phone) with the arena key, next to a kit reference; add automatic read metrics (lit top share, seam runs, silhouette IoU) with an exit code.
compose.py lighting: whole-face tone offsets (upward +1, downward -1, key-facing +1) so the lit top band exists and the lightest shade is used; a --key argument shared with the viewer and the game.

SKILL.md S1: require a kit baseline in the brief and a side-by-side at S6; state that passing every numeric gate while the atlas reads as noise is a failed round; the post-and-lintel test for when the kit wins.

piece_template.py hangers/blockout: minimum feature sizes at play size (root >= 0.3, length >= 0.8, 2 thick beat 3 thin), fuse hangers with the cut in one pass, 2-3 overlapping irregular cutters for the opening.
bake_masks.py: split cavity into crack cavity (AO <= 0.25) and contact AO (0.7, floor only, at most -1 shade).

iterations.log: Skill revised after pilot 1 (commit 45a6d72): low poly = fused form + plate displacement only (chisel 15 deg, voxel 0.08); bake_masks adds key-facing, world-position and split crack/contact AO passes; compose.py paints 6-texel cells with a per-cell lit lip and dark seam; viewer/shoot at the game's pixels per unit with a pi-W toon key; read_check.py gates the sprite read; kit.courses, fit_matrix, drop_small_shells, union-after-cut hangers; SKILL.md S1 kit baseline + post-and-lintel test, S2 hanger sizes, S6 ppu 64/36 + read_check. judge.vsCurrent: No, it does not beat the code-built cave: at ppu 64/36 it reads as a block pile at the same texel density as the kit's coursed terraces (lit lips, dark seams, 5 ramp shades, so it would sit next to them without looking foreign), but it is noisier (dark 1-2 px specks, a regular 6-texel stripe inside large facets, blocks at two competing scales) and the two forms that justified building it in Blender fail: the opening is a cramped notch under a heavy lintel mass and the stalactites are invisible stubs, so the kit's cleaner boxes still win.
strengths: Texel density is genuinely consistent (15.6-16.0 on every face) and the atlas is on the caveStone ramp with 7 colours, so the piece shares the game's pixel grid and palette; nothing reads as a smooth untextured primitive.
Lit top lips and dark bottom seams read at play size in the sprite shots (ppu 64 and 36), and chunky 8-14 texel blocks are individually readable, a clear step up from pilot 1's camouflage noise.
Course seams from kit.courses survive the SDF fuse, so the wall mass keeps the kit's stacked-stone construction logic rather than reading as a sculpted blob.
Pipeline hygiene is solid: 4,134 tris, 131 KB, 1 mesh/1 material/1 draw call, nearest sampler, meshopt only, 0 console errors, deterministic report and manifest, 11 s loop.
The pilot recorded its own bugs and workarounds (sdf_fuse UNION socket, base clamp, course overhang) in the manifest instead of hiding them.
weaknesses: The silhouette, the only reason to use Blender here, fails the brief: the opening is roughly 25% of the front area instead of the briefed ~1.5x1.6 of 3x2.4, sits low under a heavy crown, and the arch reads as a crouching M-shaped mass; the front sprite shows a heavy block with a small cutout, not a cave arch.

The three stalactites (root 0.34-0.36, length 1.05-1.15 in the blockout) are invisible at ppu 64 and 36: after the 0.08 voxel remesh, chisel and decimate they are stubs, they hang against same-shade wall interior with no contrast, and their tips nearly touch the floor so they merge with the legs.

Horizontal banding inside blocks: the final atlas was composed with cells_from 'uv grid' (a bare masks.png path was passed, so form.png's key term, pos.png's world cells and contact.png AO were all silently unused); the regular 6-texel UV grid prints a lip/seam stripe every 6 texels across every large facet.
Dark 1-2 px specks scattered over the sprite from the 12% crack-cavity rule applied per texel on a faceted low; the kit paints at most one 2x2 pit per 160 texels and never a lone dark texel.

Blocks at two scales fight each other: 14x11-texel course blocks, 6-10-texel Voronoi plates on top of them, plus chisel facets, so the sprite is busier than the kit crop and lacks its calm 3-4 value steps per block.

The compare image is apples to oranges: a graded in-game JPG crop against an ungraded viewer shot with a neutral hemisphere light; the viewer cannot show whether the piece would hold up under the game's grade.
read_check passed on seam/lip/orphan shares that say nothing about block legibility, opening size or hanger visibility, so every numeric gate was green on a piece whose hero features do not read.
skillFixes: SKILL.md S2 + piece_template.py: a numeric silhouette gate before S3 (front orthographic mask at ppu 64 from the blockout and the fused high: through-opening area >= the brief's share, each hanger >= 40 px tall with >= 4 px of background around it); document in modelling.md that cuts happen before fillet/offset and that plate growth and voxel rounding shrink an opening, so cutters must be oversized (target + fillet_iters*voxel + 1.6*plate + 2 voxels).
